name: HbA1c (Glycated Hemoglobin)
description: HbA1c (Glycated Hemoglobin) test measures the average blood glucose levels over the past 2-3 months. It reflects the percentage of hemoglobin that has become glycated (bound to glucose) and is used for diabetes diagnosis, monitoring, and management. HbA1c provides a reliable indicator of long-term glycemic control.
literatureReview: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) is a form of hemoglobin that is chemically linked to glucose. The HbA1c test measures the percentage of hemoglobin that is glycated and reflects average blood glucose levels over the previous 2-3 months. It is the gold standard for monitoring long-term glycemic control in diabetic patients and for diabetes diagnosis. HbA1c levels below 5.7% are considered normal, 5.7-6.4% indicate prediabetes, and 6.5% or higher suggest diabetes. Regular HbA1c testing helps guide treatment decisions and assess diabetes management effectiveness.
